items.headline: Isaias makes landfall on the Florida Panhandle
items.summary: Isaias grew into a Category 3 hurricane with winds up to 120 mph as it bore down on the Gulf Coast on Friday. It came ashore near Destin, Florida, and weakened as it moved inland.

items.headline: Trump agrees to buy Russian diesel in policy reversal
items.summary: President Trump said he agreed with Vladimir Putin by phone for the U.S. to obtain Russian diesel. The move reverses years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over Ukraine as the administration tries to lower fuel prices before the midterms.

items.headline: Navi Pillay wins Nobel Peace Prize as U.S. sanctions ICC
items.summary: South African jurist and former U.N. human rights chief Navi Pillay won the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize. Hours later, the Trump administration sanctioned the International Criminal Court, where she had been a judge.

items.headline: ICE agent shoots man in New York with child in car
items.summary: ICE agents shot a 28-year-old man in New York City who officials say tried to ram them with his car while a young child was in the back seat. The NYPD released bodycam footage from the aftermath, and an investigation is under way.

items.headline: Trump forms committee to investigate Fed's Lisa Cook
items.summary: President Trump set up a committee to investigate Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook in his latest effort to fire her. His memo schedules a White House hearing on Nov. 5 that it says she must attend.

items.headline: Administration freezes green cards at major tech firms
items.summary: The Trump administration suspended green card sponsorship for Microsoft and other companies. It is also investigating nine universities over alleged student exchange visa fraud.

items.headline: India detains thousands to stop youth protest
items.summary: Indian authorities detained thousands of people in New Delhi to prevent a planned mass youth protest. The demonstration targeted Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and the country's election chief.

items.headline: Katie Zacharia named White House press secretary
items.summary: President Trump named conservative commentator Katie Zacharia to replace Karoline Leavitt as White House press secretary. Zacharia has been a Trump Media adviser and a Homeland Security spokesperson.

items.headline: Fired OpenAI workers question company's safety commitment
items.summary: Three fired OpenAI employees say they were punished for raising safety concerns. OpenAI says they mishandled sensitive information.

items.headline: Fight grows over how to count corporate emissions
items.summary: An Aspen Institute report frames a debate between the Greenhouse Gas Protocol and newer e-ledger approaches to assigning responsibility for emissions. The outcome could shape how companies report and cut their climate impact.

digest.overview:
Hurricane Isaias, which reached Category 3 strength with 120 mph winds, made landfall near Destin on the Florida Panhandle and has since weakened to a post-tropical cyclone. President Trump said he agreed with Vladimir Putin to buy Russian diesel, a policy reversal aimed at lowering fuel prices before the midterms. Trump also created a committee to investigate Fed governor Lisa Cook, with a White House hearing set for Nov. 5. An ICE agent shot a man in New York City with a child in the car, and Mayor Zohran Mamdani demanded an end to ICE operations there. The administration froze green card sponsorship at Microsoft and other tech firms and opened a visa-fraud probe of nine universities. Katie Zacharia was named White House press secretary, replacing Karoline Leavitt. Arlington County, Virginia, sued to block Trump's planned arch, and former Bears coach Mike Ditka died.

Abroad, human rights lawyer Navi Pillay won the Nobel Peace Prize, and hours later Washington sanctioned the International Criminal Court, where she had been a judge. The diesel deal eases years of U.S. pressure on Moscow over the war in Ukraine, and Trump said the U.S. will not strike Iran before the midterms. Indian authorities detained thousands in New Delhi to block a youth protest against Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government and the election chief. A year after the Gaza ceasefire, Palestinians describe the truce as largely nominal. An investigation found fish farmed in China's Xinjiang region reaching the U.S. despite a forced-labor import law. On climate, an Aspen Institute report spotlights a fight over how corporate emissions are counted.

home.overview:
Cleveland and the White Sox meet tonight in a winner-take-all ALDS Game 5, with Gavin Williams facing Sean Burke for the right to open the ALCS at Tampa Bay on Monday. The Dodgers lined up Tarik Skubal and Yoshinobu Yamamoto for the first two games of the NLCS, which starts Sunday night in Milwaukee. Football mourned former Bears coach Mike Ditka. Week 5 rolls on Sunday with Eagles–Jaguars in London, 49ers–Seahawks and Ravens–Falcons under the lights, and Aaron Rodgers needs one touchdown pass against the Colts to pass Peyton Manning for third all-time including playoffs. The Knicks paused extension talks with Karl-Anthony Towns and Josh Hart ahead of the Oct. 20 NBA opener.

Club soccer came back with a jolt: Niclas Füllkrug's late goal gave Werder Bremen a 2–2 draw at Dortmund, ending BVB's perfect start, and West Ham were held 1–1 by QPR in the Championship. Saturday brings Arsenal–Leeds, Man United–Tottenham, Barcelona–Getafe and Real Madrid–Villarreal, before Man City play their first game since the guilty verdict at Liverpool on Sunday. In K League 1, FC Seoul beat Jeju SK 2–1 to go 18 points clear, while Suwon Samsung host Ansan on Sunday atop K League 2.
